text:
acme-support: Hey team — after migrating ACME's Dedicated cluster into their VPC we started seeing streaming responses cut off mid-payload. Client reconnects and we get duplicate tokens billed. Repro steps below, filing because this only happens behind their corporate proxy + onprem ingress.

emma (support): Thanks — can you paste a short curl repro and logs? Also what client library / SDK?

acme-support: Using our internal SDK (node). Quick curl to simulate:```curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer REQ_TOKEN\" \"https://private.redwood.acme/api/v1/streams?model=text-xxx\" -d \"{\'prompt\':\'hello\'}\"``` We see: initial SSE lines then abrupt 

[STREAM] data: {"delta":"Hello"}
[STREAM] data: {"delta":" world"}
[STREAM] data: [TRUNCATED]

Then client reconnects and receives resume with overlapping tokens.

jon (eng-runtime): Do you have full raw TCP capture or TLS-level logs from their ingress? If MTU fragmentation or proxy chunking is reordering we might see partial TLS records or PSM (proxy split) behavior.

acme-support: We captured nginx-ingress logs and the corporate proxy (BlueGate) logs. Attaching snippets:```nginx: recv_len=1500, write_len=1400, flags=0\nproxy: chunked=true, seq=1372, dropped=0, ack-gap=16``` Not sure how to share full pcap here.

sara (networking): The recv/write numbers look like PMTU/MSS effects. If the proxy is chopping SSE frames mid-event and then reordering under load, the client sees a truncated event. Does the client support event-stream resumption? Also which keepalive interval?

acme-support: Keepalive=30s default. Client tries to reconnect with If-None-Match header with resume-token from last event. But we see a 401 on the resume attempt occasionally.

emma (support): 401 on resume could be token rotation/short-lived tokens issue. Are you rotating tokens server-side on reconnect? Token TTL for ACME service?

acme-support: Token TTL is 60s for their internal gateway, but our SDK tries to refresh transparently. We suspect race: proxy delays then token expires when client hits resume endpoint.

tim (eng-oncall): Two separate faults: (1) mid-payload truncation (likely network/proxy MTU/chunking) (2) resume 401 (auth/session race) causing duplicate billing when client retries without resume acceptance. Prioritize repro: we need a deterministic script that reproduces both in a short run.

jon (eng-runtime): Agreed. Can you run a repro that: 1) streams a 10k token response, 2) simulates MTU 1200 at proxy, 3) injects a 120-300ms re-order window? If you can't simulate, provide a tcpdump. Also include exact SSE bytes around the cut.

acme-support: I can run a repro container. Quick notes: their proxy enforces 1200 PMTU and has a per-conn buffer of 8KB. I can reproduce ~1/10 streams with truncation in our test cluster.

sara (networking): For diagnostics try: 1) set client keepalive to 10s, 2) force shorter token TTL to reproduce 401, 3) run h2c passthrough to bypass proxy to confirm. Also capture the SSE boundary bytes: look for "\n\n" delimiter between events. If the proxy strips or splits that sequence across packets, client reconstructor may drop partial event.

acme-support: When we bypass the corporate proxy, stream is stable. So definitely the proxy. But bypassing for production isn't an option.

jon (eng-runtime): Two mitigation paths: A) Make the server emit more granular flushes (smaller SSE events) so proxy doesn't split the delimiter across MTU boundary. B) Improve resume semantics: server should accept resume tokens that are within a small overlapped window and deduplicate by event-id to avoid billing duplicates.

emma (support): Can you try server side change A quickly? Jon, any config we can toggle in Dedicated to reduce per-event size or add padding to align boundaries?

jon (eng-runtime): We can add a soft option to force max SSE chunk size (e.g., 800 bytes) or emit a zero-width ping event every 500 bytes to keep the delimiter intact. I'll push a canary flag to the customer's dedicated pool for debugging.

tim (eng-oncall): Also we need to address 401 on resume: support, please ask ACME to log the resume request headers so we can verify token value, expiry, and time skew. If token TTL is 60s and proxy delays 30-40s, race is plausible. Consider allowing a short grace window for resume call (e.g., accept tokens expired <=30s if accompanied by original session id).

acme-support: We'll add logging for resume headers. Also trying Jon's smaller chunk experiment now.

(30m later)

acme-support: Verified: after forcing SSE chunk size to <=800 bytes, truncation stops in our tests. Also resume 401 rate dropped because the smaller chunks reduced perceived latency; still some 401s occasionally.

emma (support): Good. Next steps: 1) Jon to propose a server-side mitigation (feature flag) for forcing smaller SSE writes or interleaved pings. 2) Tim + Jon to propose resume-token grace policy to avoid billing duplicates. 3) Sara to work with ACME's proxy vendor for a config change (preserve SSE event boundaries / increase MTU). 4) ACME to provide tcpdump for one failing run.

jon (eng-runtime): I'll open an internal RFC and a short-lived canary rollout for the forced-chunk-size flag. Will include metrics to track truncated-event errors and duplicate billing incidents.

sara (networking): I'll draft a config snippet to request from BlueGate: set proxy_streaming_preserve_delimiters on; set max_chunk_size 1400; enable tcp_nodelay. Recommend ACME try bumping MTU on their ingress if possible.

acme-support: Thanks—we'll send the tcpdump and try the vendor change. Appreciate the quick turnaround. :thumbsup:

emma (support): Picking this up as P0 until we have vendor confirmation or the canary reduces incidents below baseline. I'll keep the ticket open and update ACME.

infra-bot: deploy-canary:jon/force-sse-chunk-size -> started on acme-dedicated-pool-3

jon (eng-runtime): Canary started. Will report back with logs and metrics.

acme-support: Will run load for next 4 hours and post any failing traces.

emma (support): Thanks everyone. If anyone gets a tcpdump/pcap please drop to the ticket thread.
